title: Six weeks with Earl Hines in San Francisco, 1955
summary: Ed Garland arranges a job and Watkins opens on Labor Day with Hines, Darnell Howard and Garland, then is replaced by Earl Watkins.

story.theme_name: Going west: California and the Los Angeles scene
story.community_name: Going west: moving to and working in California

blocks.x: Well things that got kind of tough with me around 1955, Doc was getting up a house band. Well he had, what's his bass player, he used to play with Ori. Barlin Burden.

Oh, Ed Garlin, yeah. Well Ed Garlin had wrote me a letter and asked me about playing well and I told him he asked me because our band wasn't doing anything and I was willing to, you know, take the job until I could make a pretty good salary. So Doc had called me on long distance phone and told me, asked me how I'm ready if I wanted to come by plane or by train. I told him not before to come by train. So he sent me a ticket and I went on out there and that was August, the latter part of August 1955. Yeah. Because I opened up on a Labor Day night with Earl Hines. Oh yeah, you were playing with Earl Hines. So I played out there six weeks with Earl.
Who else was in the band then?

Earl had Ed Garlin, Earl Hines, and this little white trumpet player there, I can't think of his name. Muggsy was it? No, it wasn't Muggsy Spaniel, no. Another little trumpet player, he's pretty bad off sick now if he ain't dead now. He's out there in San Francisco. And we had this clarinet player, Donnell Howard. Oh man. Our clarinet. We only had a six piece lineup. Earl Hines, Donnell Howard, Ed Garlin, myself. You were on trombone. And Lil' Jimmy.
Jimmy Archie? Lil' Jimmy Archie, yeah.

He was on trombone. I think he's still with Earl Hines, if I'm not mistaken. But he wasn't on that concert at Monterey, I think he was still at Muggsy Spaniel at the Hangover. Yeah. So you worked there for what, six weeks? See I worked with him for six weeks and they got this boy Earl Watkins to take my place. Because see my type of drumming and Earl's type of music didn't fit in together. See because I was, just like I said, I was more on the authentic side than what he was. Because he was kind of swinging his band more, you know.
And this Earl Watkins was playing the more modern stuff.

Yeah, he was playing the modern stuff. So naturally hired him, which didn't make me angry at all because I just had an idea I wasn't going to make it after the first two weeks with him. You know, I just didn't watch this. You're watching this is it. You just working on Back to the Army. Well, George was out there when I started playing with him. Yeah, Lawrence's cousin Si on drums then. Si Frazier?
